notes: Bundled at /assets/regions/us_states.json. Loaded into the PlateRegion table on first run. Compare data_version with stored value on app start to apply updates without schema migration.

regions.name: Alabama
regions.motto: Audemus jura nostra defendere (We dare defend our rights)
fun_facts: Alabama was the first state to recognize Christmas as an official holiday, doing so in 1836.
The world's first electric trolley system began operation in Montgomery in 1886.
Helen Keller was born in Tuscumbia, Alabama in 1880.

regions.name: Alaska
fun_facts: Alaska is the largest U.S. state by area — more than twice the size of Texas.
It has more coastline than all other U.S. states combined.
The United States purchased Alaska from Russia in 1867 for about 2 cents per acre.

regions.name: Arizona
fun_facts: The Grand Canyon is one of the Seven Natural Wonders of the World.
Arizona produces enough copper each year to lead the nation in production.
The original London Bridge was bought and reassembled in Lake Havasu City in 1971.

regions.name: Arkansas
fun_facts: Arkansas is the only U.S. state that produces diamonds — Crater of Diamonds State Park lets visitors keep what they find.
Hot Springs National Park is the smallest national park and one of the oldest federally protected areas in the U.S.
Walmart was founded in Bentonville, Arkansas in 1962.

regions.name: California
fun_facts: California is home to both the highest and lowest points in the contiguous U.S. — Mount Whitney and Death Valley.
It would be the fifth-largest economy in the world if it were its own country.
Coast redwoods in California are the tallest trees on Earth, with some growing over 380 feet tall.

regions.name: Colorado
fun_facts: Colorado has the highest mean elevation of any U.S. state.
The cheeseburger was reportedly invented in Denver in 1935.
Colorado has more than 50 mountain peaks that rise above 14,000 feet.

regions.name: Connecticut
regions.motto: Qui transtulit sustinet (He who transplanted sustains)
fun_facts: The first hamburger in the U.S. was reportedly served at Louis' Lunch in New Haven in 1900.
Connecticut is nicknamed the Constitution State and home to the first written constitution in the colonies, the Fundamental Orders of 1638.
The first telephone book ever published contained only 50 names and was issued in New Haven in 1878.

regions.name: Delaware
fun_facts: Delaware was the first state to ratify the U.S. Constitution, on December 7, 1787 — earning it the nickname The First State.
It is the second-smallest U.S. state by area.
Delaware has no sales tax.

regions.name: Florida
fun_facts: Florida has the longest coastline of any state in the contiguous U.S.
It is the only state that borders both the Atlantic Ocean and the Gulf of Mexico.
St. Augustine, founded in 1565, is the oldest continuously inhabited European-established settlement in the U.S.

regions.name: Georgia
fun_facts: Georgia is the leading producer of peaches, peanuts, and pecans in the U.S.
Coca-Cola was invented in Atlanta in 1886 by pharmacist John Pemberton.
Georgia was the fourth state to ratify the U.S. Constitution.

regions.name: Hawaii
regions.motto: Ua Mau ke Ea o ka 'Aina i ka Pono (The life of the land is perpetuated in righteousness)
fun_facts: Hawaii is the only U.S. state made entirely of islands.
It is the most isolated population center on Earth, more than 2,000 miles from the nearest continent.
Hawaii is the only state with two official languages: English and Hawaiian.

regions.name: Idaho
fun_facts: Idaho produces about one-third of all potatoes grown in the U.S.
Hells Canyon, on the Idaho-Oregon border, is the deepest river gorge in North America — deeper than the Grand Canyon.
Idaho was the 43rd state admitted to the Union in 1890.

regions.name: Illinois
fun_facts: The world's first skyscraper, the Home Insurance Building, was built in Chicago in 1885.
Abraham Lincoln practiced law and launched his political career in Illinois.
Illinois is home to the largest cookie and cracker factory in the world, Nabisco's bakery in Chicago.

regions.name: Indiana
fun_facts: The Indianapolis 500, first run in 1911, is one of the oldest auto races in the world.
Indiana is one of only two states with a non-rectangular flag — its state flag features a torch and stars.
The first long-distance auto race in the U.S. was held in Indiana in 1909.

regions.name: Iowa
regions.motto: Our liberties we prize and our rights we will maintain
fun_facts: Iowa is the only state whose east and west borders are formed entirely by rivers — the Mississippi and the Missouri.
Iowa produces more corn than any other state, and more than most countries.
The Iowa caucuses are traditionally the first contest in the U.S. presidential primary season.

regions.name: Kansas
regions.motto: Ad astra per aspera (To the stars through difficulties)
fun_facts: The geographic center of the contiguous 48 states is located near Lebanon, Kansas.
Kansas is one of the world's leading wheat producers.
Dodge City, Kansas is the windiest city in the U.S. on average.

regions.name: Kentucky
regions.motto: United we stand, divided we fall
fun_facts: About 95 percent of the world's bourbon is produced in Kentucky.
The Kentucky Derby, first run in 1875, is the oldest continuously held sporting event in the U.S.
Mammoth Cave is the longest known cave system in the world, with more than 400 miles of explored passageways.

regions.name: Louisiana
fun_facts: Louisiana is the only U.S. state with parishes instead of counties.
New Orleans is the birthplace of jazz music.
Louisiana's legal system is based on Napoleonic Code, unlike any other U.S. state.

regions.name: Maine
fun_facts: Maine produces about 90 percent of the lobster supply in the U.S.
Maine is the only state whose name has exactly one syllable.
Maine has more coastline than California, despite being much smaller.

regions.name: Maryland
regions.motto: Fatti maschii, parole femine (Strong deeds, gentle words)
fun_facts: The U.S. national anthem, The Star-Spangled Banner, was written by Francis Scott Key during the Battle of Baltimore in 1814.
The U.S. Naval Academy is located in Annapolis.
Maryland is home to Old Bay seasoning, created in Baltimore in the 1940s.

regions.name: Massachusetts
regions.motto: Ense petit placidam sub libertate quietem (By the sword we seek peace, but peace only under liberty)
fun_facts: Harvard University, founded in 1636, is the oldest institution of higher learning in the U.S.
The first public park in America, Boston Common, was established in 1634.
Basketball and volleyball were both invented in Massachusetts.

regions.name: Michigan
regions.motto: Si quaeris peninsulam amoenam circumspice (If you seek a pleasant peninsula, look about you)
fun_facts: Michigan is the only U.S. state made up of two separate peninsulas.
Michigan borders four of the five Great Lakes — only Lake Ontario is missing.
Detroit is known as the Motor City and birthplace of the American auto industry.

regions.name: Minnesota
regions.motto: L'Étoile du Nord (The Star of the North)
fun_facts: Minnesota is known as the Land of 10,000 Lakes — though it actually has more than 11,000.
The Mall of America in Bloomington is one of the largest shopping malls in the U.S.
Minnesota produces more turkeys than any other state.

regions.name: Mississippi
regions.motto: Virtute et armis (By valor and arms)
fun_facts: The teddy bear was named after President Theodore Roosevelt following a hunting trip in Mississippi in 1902.
Root beer was invented in Biloxi in 1898.
The Mississippi River, the second-longest river in North America, borders the state.

regions.name: Missouri
regions.motto: Salus populi suprema lex esto (The welfare of the people shall be the supreme law)
fun_facts: The Gateway Arch in St. Louis is the tallest monument in the U.S. at 630 feet.
Missouri shares borders with eight states, tied with Tennessee for the most.
The ice cream cone is said to have been invented at the 1904 World's Fair in St. Louis.

regions.name: Montana
fun_facts: Montana is nicknamed Big Sky Country for its wide open landscapes.
Glacier National Park in Montana is part of the world's first International Peace Park, shared with Canada.
Montana has the largest grizzly bear population in the lower 48 states.

regions.name: Nebraska
fun_facts: Nebraska has the only unicameral (single-house) state legislature in the U.S.
Kool-Aid was invented in Hastings, Nebraska in 1927 and is the official state soft drink.
The Sandhills region of Nebraska is the largest sand dune formation in the Western Hemisphere.

regions.name: Nevada
fun_facts: Nevada is the driest state in the U.S., averaging just over 9 inches of rain per year.
About 86 percent of Nevada's land is owned by the federal government — the highest of any state.
Las Vegas has more hotel rooms than any other city in the world.

regions.name: New Hampshire
fun_facts: New Hampshire holds the first primary election in U.S. presidential races.
It was the first colony to declare its independence from England, in January 1776.
New Hampshire has the shortest ocean coastline of any state with coastline — just 18 miles.

regions.name: New Jersey
fun_facts: New Jersey has the highest population density of any U.S. state.
The first organized baseball game was played in Hoboken in 1846.
Thomas Edison's lab in Menlo Park produced the phonograph, the light bulb, and the motion picture camera.

regions.name: New Mexico
regions.motto: Crescit eundo (It grows as it goes)
fun_facts: New Mexico has the highest percentage of Hispanic Americans of any state.
Santa Fe, founded in 1610, is the oldest state capital in the U.S.
The world's first atomic bomb was detonated at the Trinity Site in New Mexico in 1945.

regions.name: New York
fun_facts: New York City has more than 800 languages spoken, making it the most linguistically diverse city in the world.
The first U.S. capital was New York City, where George Washington was inaugurated in 1789.
New York's subway system has 472 stations — more than any other system in the world.

regions.name: North Carolina
regions.motto: Esse quam videri (To be, rather than to seem)
fun_facts: The Wright brothers made the first powered airplane flight at Kitty Hawk in 1903, though they designed and built their aircraft in Dayton, Ohio.
North Carolina is the leading producer of sweet potatoes in the U.S.
The first state university in the U.S. opened here in 1795 — the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill.

regions.name: North Dakota
regions.motto: Liberty and union, now and forever, one and inseparable
fun_facts: North Dakota is one of the least visited and least populated states in the U.S.
It is the leading producer of honey in the country.
The geographic center of North America is in Rugby, North Dakota.

regions.name: Ohio
regions.motto: With God, all things are possible
fun_facts: Seven U.S. presidents were born in Ohio, more than any other state except Virginia.
Cincinnati hosted the first professional baseball team, the Red Stockings, in 1869.
The Wright brothers, inventors of the airplane, were from Dayton, Ohio.

regions.name: Oklahoma
fun_facts: Oklahoma has more man-made lakes than any other state — over 200.
The shopping cart was invented in Ardmore, Oklahoma in 1937.
Oklahoma has the largest Native American population of any U.S. state.

regions.name: Oregon
regions.motto: Alis volat propriis (She flies with her own wings)
fun_facts: Crater Lake is the deepest lake in the U.S., at 1,943 feet.
Oregon's state flag is the only U.S. state flag with different designs on its two sides.
Hells Canyon, on the Oregon-Idaho border, is the deepest river gorge in North America.

regions.name: Pennsylvania
fun_facts: The Declaration of Independence and the U.S. Constitution were both signed in Philadelphia.
Hershey, Pennsylvania is known as the Chocolate Capital of the U.S.
Pennsylvania was the second state to ratify the U.S. Constitution.

regions.name: Rhode Island
fun_facts: Rhode Island is the smallest U.S. state by area.
It has the longest official name of any state: State of Rhode Island and Providence Plantations (shortened in 2020 to just State of Rhode Island).
The first fully automated post office in the U.S. opened in Providence in 1960.

regions.name: South Carolina
regions.motto: Dum spiro spero (While I breathe, I hope)
fun_facts: Charleston is one of the oldest cities in the U.S., founded in 1670.
The first shots of the Civil War were fired at Fort Sumter in Charleston Harbor in 1861.
South Carolina is the leading producer of peaches on the East Coast, ahead of Georgia.

regions.name: South Dakota
fun_facts: Mount Rushmore features 60-foot-tall sculpted faces of four U.S. presidents.
South Dakota is home to Badlands National Park, with its dramatic eroded rock formations.
Sturgis hosts one of the largest motorcycle rallies in the world each August.

regions.name: Tennessee
fun_facts: Nashville is known as Music City and home to the Grand Ole Opry, the longest-running radio broadcast in U.S. history.
Tennessee borders eight states, tied with Missouri for the most.
Great Smoky Mountains National Park, which Tennessee shares with North Carolina, is the most-visited national park in the U.S.

regions.name: Texas
fun_facts: Texas is the only U.S. state to have been an independent country before joining the Union.
It is the second-largest state by area and second-largest by population.
The King Ranch in Texas is larger than the state of Rhode Island.

regions.name: Utah
fun_facts: Utah has five national parks, more than any state except California and Alaska.
The Great Salt Lake is the largest saltwater lake in the Western Hemisphere.
Utah has the highest literacy rate in the U.S.

regions.name: Vermont
fun_facts: Vermont is the leading producer of maple syrup in the U.S.
Montpelier is the only U.S. state capital without a McDonald's.
Vermont was the first state admitted to the Union after the original 13 colonies.

regions.name: Virginia
regions.motto: Sic semper tyrannis (Thus always to tyrants)
fun_facts: Eight U.S. presidents were born in Virginia — more than any other state.
Jamestown, founded in 1607, was the first permanent English settlement in the Americas.
The Pentagon, the world's largest office building by floor area, is located in Arlington.

regions.name: Washington
fun_facts: Washington is the only U.S. state named after a president.
Mount Rainier in Washington is the most glaciated peak in the contiguous U.S.
Seattle is home to the original Starbucks, which opened in Pike Place Market in 1971.

regions.name: West Virginia
regions.motto: Montani semper liberi (Mountaineers are always free)
fun_facts: West Virginia was formed by breaking away from Virginia during the Civil War, becoming the only state to be admitted that way.
Almost the entire state is covered by the Appalachian Mountains.
The New River Gorge Bridge was once the longest steel arch bridge in the world.

regions.name: Wisconsin
fun_facts: Wisconsin is the leading producer of cheese in the U.S.
The ice cream sundae was reportedly invented in Two Rivers, Wisconsin in 1881.
Wisconsin has over 15,000 lakes.

regions.name: Wyoming
fun_facts: Wyoming is the least populated U.S. state.
Yellowstone, mostly in Wyoming, was the world's first national park, established in 1872.
Wyoming was the first U.S. territory or state to grant women the right to vote, in 1869.
